text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Crown Prince and Prime Minister Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al-Sabah in good condition and recovering in Britain. Sheikh Saad flew to London on Monday for follow up treatment after undergoing colon surgery in Kuwait on Saturday.

- Emir of Qatar Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa al-Thani says Doha does not apply double standards in dealing with Kuwait. Qatar, which has full diplomatic ties with Kuwait's former occupier Iraq, is among Kuwait's Gulf Arab allies with direct links with Iraqi President Saddam Hussein.
- Interior Minister Sheikh Mohammad Khaled al-Sabah says some 100 Iraqis held in a deportation centre refuse to return home.
- Sri Lanka wants Kuwait to finance investment projects.

- Iran's Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati will visit Kuwait next week to invite Emir of Kuwait Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah to a summit in Iran in December of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference (OIC).
- Kuwait Stock Exchange index drops 2.5 points on Tuesday to 2,238 points.
